title: 02. Ingestion & Chunking: Sliding Window Chunking
summary: Sliding window chunking creates chunks with significant overlap by sliding a fixed-size window across the document at a configurable step size.

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body: Sliding window chunking creates chunks with significant overlap by sliding a fixed-size window across the document at a configurable step size. Unlike the typical 10-20% overlap in fixed-size chunking, sliding window can use 50%+ overlap, ensuring that every possible N-gram of text appears in at least one chunk. This maximizes retrieval recall at the cost of significant storage increase and embedding cost. It's most appropriate for dense technical content where any sentence might be critical (e.g., legal contracts, medical literature), but impractical for large corpora due to the storage multiplier (2x-10x more chunks than fixed splitting).

sections.title: ② Key Code
sections.body:
```python
from typing import List, Iterator
from langchain_core.documents import Document
import tiktoken

def sliding_window_chunks(
    text: str,
    window_tokens: int = 512,
    step_tokens: int = 256,  # 50% overlap
    model: str = "text-embedding-3-large"
) -> Iterator[str]:
    """
    Generate chunks using sliding window with configurable step size.
    step_tokens < window_tokens creates overlap.
    """
    enc = tiktoken.encoding_for_model(model)
    tokens = enc.encode(text)
    
    pos = 0
    while pos < len(tokens):
        window = tokens[pos:pos + window_tokens]
        chunk_text = enc.decode(window)
        yield chunk_text
        
        pos += step_tokens  # slide by step_tokens
        
        # Stop if we've covered everything
        if pos + step_tokens > len(tokens):
            # Final chunk
            final_window = tokens[pos:]
            if final_window:
                yield enc.decode(final_window)
            break

def sliding_window_documents(
    docs: List[Document],
    window_tokens: int = 512,
    step_tokens: int = 256,
) -> List[Document]:
    """Apply sliding window chunking to a list of documents."""
    result = []
    for doc in docs:
        for i, chunk_text in enumerate(sliding_window_chunks(
            doc.page_content, window_tokens, step_tokens
        )):
            result.append(Document(
                page_content=chunk_text,
                metadata={
                    **doc.metadata,
                    "chunk_index": i,
                    "window_size": window_tokens,
                    "step_size": step_tokens,
                    "overlap_ratio": 1 - (step_tokens / window_tokens)
                }
            ))
    return result

# Cost analysis for sliding window
def sliding_window_cost_analysis(
    doc_tokens: int,
    window_tokens: int = 512,
    step_tokens: int = 256,
    cost_per_1m_tokens: float = 0.02  # text-embedding-3-small pricing
) -> dict:
    """Calculate embedding cost for sliding window vs fixed chunking."""
    
    # Number of chunks
    num_sliding_chunks = max(1, (doc_tokens - window_tokens) // step_tokens + 1)
    num_fixed_chunks = max(1, doc_tokens // window_tokens)
    
    # Total tokens to embed
    sliding_embed_tokens = num_sliding_chunks * window_tokens
    fixed_embed_tokens = doc_tokens
    
    sliding_cost = (sliding_embed_tokens / 1_000_000) * cost_per_1m_tokens
    fixed_cost = (fixed_embed_tokens / 1_000_000) * cost_per_1m_tokens
    
    return {
        "fixed_chunks": num_fixed_chunks,
        "sliding_chunks": num_sliding_chunks,
        "chunk_multiplier": num_sliding_chunks / num_fixed_chunks,
        "fixed_embed_tokens": fixed_embed_tokens,
        "sliding_embed_tokens": sliding_embed_tokens,
        "fixed_cost_usd": fixed_cost,
        "sliding_cost_usd": sliding_cost,
        "cost_multiplier": sliding_cost / fixed_cost
    }
```

```
                 |──────────|──────────|──────────|
Chunk 1:         |===512 tokens===|
Chunk 2:              |===512 tokens===|
Chunk 3:                   |===512 tokens===|
Chunk 4:                        |===512 tokens===|
Overlap: 256 tokens (50%)

Every position appears in 2 chunks → no context is ever fully cut

USE CASE COMPARISON:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Strategy          Storage Cost  Retrieval Recall  Use When
Fixed (0% overlap)    1x           Low             Large corpora, cost-sensitive
Fixed (20% overlap)   1.3x         Medium          General purpose (default)
Sliding (50% overlap) 2x           High            Dense technical content
Sliding (75% overlap) 4x           Very High       Legal, medical (critical accuracy)

WHEN TO USE SLIDING WINDOW:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
✓ Legal contracts (every clause is critical)
✓ Medical literature (precision matters over cost)
✓ Regulatory compliance documents
✗ Large web corpora (too expensive)
✗ FAQ databases (short documents, no need)
✗ Real-time ingestion (too slow)
```
